common: Difficulty comes from rarity and depth, not jargon, obscure names, extra dates, or longer wording. Use clear eighth-grade English and explain necessary terms. Keep the assigned sentence count; exclude definitions, overviews, and familiar facts without a distinctive detail.
easyEvidence: Prefer a relevant inner section; an introduction qualifies only for a specific detail. Use at most two adjacent paragraphs; exclude basic topic introductions.
innerEvidence: Use one named non-lead section and at most two adjacent paragraphs; exclude the lead and infobox and keep all sentence evidence in that section.
levels: Choose an accessible, specific detail with one straightforward relationship. Require no specialist background and explain necessary terms immediately.
Choose a less familiar detail about a recognizable subject, requiring little background. Explain its main relationship directly.
Choose a particular incident or mechanism with a clear explanation of what happened and its distinguishing detail.
Choose an unfamiliar detail involving an important condition, decision, or consequence; explain how that detail matters to this fact.
Choose a less commonly discussed event or mechanism whose distinguishing detail requires explanation. Go beyond standard examples and well-known trivia.
Choose a narrower result, exception, or decision and explain, when supported, why it differs from the usual case. Avoid a familiar fact with extra background.
Choose a specialist detail involving a particular experiment, document, design choice, or mechanism, not a general description of that subject.
Choose a niche exception or subtle relationship within specialist material. Center the fact on its specific qualification or mechanism rather than the better-known surrounding story.
Choose a highly obscure detail distinguished by a specific circumstance, limitation, or documented result. Exclude familiar introductory facts and commonly repeated specialist examples.

Choose an exceptionally obscure, tightly bounded detail within an already specialized subject. Center a documented circumstance, limitation, exception, or result; exclude famous trivia, standard examples, and whole-section summaries. A rare name or date alone is insufficient.
